claims: 7-Eleven is closing 645 underperforming stores across North America during the 2026 fiscal year.
7-Eleven's fiscal 2026 is from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027.
7-Eleven will have a net loss of 440 stores.
7-Eleven's store closures are driven by declining traffic, inflation, and lower cigarette sales.
7-Eleven's store closures are part of a restructuring to shift focus toward larger, food-focused stores and away from traditional small kiosks.
7-Eleven's decision to close stores is due to underperforming locations, falling sales, inflationary pressure, and a significant drop in cigarette purchases.
7-Eleven's closures are part of a long-term plan to pivot toward food-forward stores that prioritize fresh food, hot meals, and beverage options.
7-Eleven's food-forward stores compete with chains like Wawa and Sheetz.
Some of 7-Eleven's closed stores will be converted into wholesale fuel stores.
Wholesale fuel stores operate without the retail staff and overhead of a full convenience store.
7-Eleven's current move marks the fifth consecutive year that 7-Eleven has closed more stores than it has opened.
7-Eleven has not released a public list of the specific stores scheduled for closure.
